ing: for cooking the beans, plus more as needed
st: Put the soaked, drained beans in a medium pot with [[3 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, for about 60 minutes until the beans are tender.
Check the water level now and then and top up with hot water so the beans stay just covered.
When the beans are soft, stir in the coconut milk, onion, garlic, thyme, whole pepper (if using), [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper.
Measure the liquid in the pot. You need about [[4 cups]] total; add water or drain a little to get there.
Bring the pot to a boil, then stir in the rinsed rice.
Let it return to a boil, then cover with a tight lid and turn the heat to the lowest setting.
Cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Turn off the heat and let it sit covered for 5 minutes.
Remove the thyme stems and the whole pepper, fluff with a fork, and serve with stew chicken or fried fish.

ing: annatto paste; or 2 tbsp paprika plus 1 tbsp white vinegar
st: In a large bowl, mix the recado paste with [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, [[1 tsp]] pepper, [[1 tsp]] oregano, [[1 tsp]] salt and the garlic.
Add the chicken and rub the paste into every piece. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil with [[1 tbsp]] brown sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat until the sugar melts and turns deep brown.
Add the chicken in a single layer and brown it for about 5 minutes per side, working in batches if needed.
Add the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil if the pot looks dry, then add the onion and bell pepper. Cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in [[2 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender.
Uncover and simmer 5 more minutes to thicken the gravy. Check that the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Serve over rice and beans with potato salad or fried plantain.
Whisk [[3 cups]] flour, [[1.5 tsp]] baking powder, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] sugar in a large bowl.
Rub the cold butter into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Pour in [[0.75 cup]] warm milk a little at a time, mixing until a soft dough forms. Add a splash more milk only if it is dry.
Knead on a floured surface for 2 minutes until smooth. Cover the dough with a towel and rest it for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 balls. Roll each into a circle about 0.25 inch thick and cut into 4 triangles.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a deep, heavy pot to 350°F (175°C). A pinch of dough should sizzle right away.
Fry the triangles a few at a time for about 1 to 2 minutes per side. They should puff up and turn golden brown.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm with refried beans, eggs, cheese, or honey or jam.

ing: snapper or similar, cut in chunks
st: Rub the fish with the lime juice and [[1 tsp]] salt. Set aside in the fridge.
Bring [[4 cups]] water to a boil in a large pot and add the green plantains, cut into 3 pieces each. Boil for 25 minutes until very soft.
Move the plantains to a bowl, keeping about [[1 cup]] of the cooking water. Mash them with a sturdy pestle or masher, adding a splash of the water, until smooth and sticky. Shape into balls.
Cover the mashed plantain loosely to keep it warm.
In a wide pot, combine the coconut milk, onion, garlic, thyme, whole pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer the sauce for 15 minutes so the flavors blend.
Add the fish chunks and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Remove the thyme stems and the whole pepper.
Serve the fish and broth in bowls with a mound of mashed plantain on the side or in the middle.
Toss the cabbage with [[2 tbsp]] vinegar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Let it sit for 10 minutes.
Soak the sliced onion and chopped chili in a little extra vinegar if you like it sharp. Drain before using.
Warm the refried beans in a small pot over low heat, adding a spoonful of water if thick.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry the tortillas one at a time for about 1 minute per side until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towels.
Spread each crisp tortilla with beans.
Top with a pinch of cheese, then the pickled cabbage, onion and chili.
Serve right away while the shells are crunchy.

ing: for frying, plus 1 tbsp for filling
st: Stir the masa harina with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[1.25 cups]] warm water. Knead until it feels like soft play dough, then cover.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, tomato and chili for 3 minutes.
Stir in the flaked cooked fish, the recado paste and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cook 3 minutes more, then cool slightly.
Divide the dough into 12 balls. Press each between two pieces of plastic into a circle about 4 inches wide.
Put a spoonful of filling on one half of each circle. Fold over and press the edges closed, sealing well.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the turnovers in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with hot sauce and pickled onions.
Simmer the chicken in [[3 cups]] water with [[0.5 tsp]] salt for 18 minutes, until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Shred it with two forks.
Toss the onion and cabbage with [[2 tbsp]] vinegar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Let stand while you make the dough.
Mix the masa harina, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[1.25 cups]] warm water into a soft dough. Cover it.
Roll the dough into 12 balls. Flatten each to a disc about 3 inches wide and 0.25 inch thick.
Heat [[1.5 cups]] oil in a skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the discs a few at a time, about 1 minute per side, until puffed and light golden.
Drain the salbutes on paper towels.
Top each salbute with shredded chicken, cabbage and onion, tomato and avocado slices.
Serve right away with hot sauce.
Put the eggs in a pot, cover with cold water, boil for 10 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
In a large pot, bring [[8 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt to a boil. Add the cassava and boil 15 minutes.
Add the plantains and sweet potatoes and boil 15 minutes more, until all are fork-tender.
While those cook, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper. Simmer 15 minutes to make a thick sauce.
Season the fish with a pinch of salt and add it to the sauce. Cover and cook 8 minutes until it flakes.
Drain the vegetables well and arrange on a platter with the eggs and fish.
Spoon the tomato sauce over everything and serve hot.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tbsp]] baking powder, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in the raisins until evenly spread.
Pour in [[0.75 cup]] milk and mix until a soft dough forms. Do not overwork it.
Scoop the dough into 10 rounds on the baking sheet, spacing them 2 inches apart.
Brush the tops with beaten egg.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool on a rack for 10 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature, with coffee.
